common_name: Heart to Heart White Star Caladium (Blushing White Fancy-Leaf Caladium)
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart White Star'

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil stays reliably above 65F; in zone 9 plant April-June. White Star is a patented Classic Caladiums introduction (Dr. Robert Hartman) bred for brighter-light tolerance than older white fancy-leaf cultivars.

directions: Plant tubers in warm, moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in part sun to shade once nights stay reliably above 60 degrees F. White Star opens soothing white with a shy pink blush and a deep crimson blaze radiating from the base of each leaf, and the white blade slowly takes on a faint rosy tint as the foliage matures through the season. This Heart to Heart series selection tolerates brighter exposure than older white fancy-leaf types without scorching, making it useful for brightening a shaded bed that gets a few hours of direct sun. Mulch to conserve moisture and dig tubers before the first fall frost outside the warmest zones.

common_name: Heart to Heart Dawn to Dusk Caladium (Cream and Red Multi-Color Caladium)
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Dawn to Dusk'

planting.note: Plant tubers after soil has warmed above 65F in late spring; in zone 9 plant April-June. Dawn to Dusk was previously marketed under the name Creamsickle.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to sun once the soil has warmed in late spring. Dawn to Dusk carries a soft cream-white center splashed with red freckling and framed by a clean green margin, giving a warmer, softer multi-color effect than the typical bold red-and-green pattern. Its sun tolerance lets it hold color in brighter spots than most fancy-leaf caladiums, while still performing well in traditional shade plantings. Lift and store tubers indoors over winter outside the warmest zones, replanting the following spring once temperatures warm.

common_name: Heart to Heart Flatter Me Caladium (Green-and-Red Patchwork Caladium)
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Flatter Me'

planting.note: Plant tubers 1-2 inches deep after soil has warmed in spring; Flatter Me grows taller than most Heart to Heart series caladiums and benefits from a bit more spacing.

directions: Plant tubers 1-2 inches deep in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to sun after the soil has warmed in spring. Flatter Me produces a patchwork of light and dark green splotches threaded with red veining across each leaf, a busier, more textured multi-color pattern than solid-centered caladiums, and it grows taller than most Heart to Heart introductions. The extra height makes it a good choice for the back of a mixed shade planting or as a thriller in a large container. Keep soil consistently moist through the growing season and dig tubers for winter storage where temperatures drop below the mid-50s.

common_name: Water's Edge Caladium (White Fancy-Leaf Sun-Tolerant Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil is reliably warm; Water's Edge is a Classic Caladiums introduction bred for an upright habit and brighter-light tolerance.

directions: Plant tubers in warm, moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to sun, siting it where the bright foliage can be appreciated from a distance. Water's Edge is a fancy-leaf white caladium with an upright growth habit and leaves that stay crisp white from the center outward, giving strong brightness in dim corners of the garden. Its tolerance for several hours of direct sun makes it more versatile than many white caladiums, which often scorch outside deep shade. Provide even moisture through summer and lift tubers before frost in all but the mildest winter climates.

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil is reliably warm; Monument is an introduction from the White Christmas breeding line and shows best in deeper shade than sun-tolerant caladiums.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade, where its bright white leaves with a deep green border show best against darker companions. Monument is an introduction from the White Christmas breeding line and shares that cultivar's luminous white coloring, but its leaf edges often develop a lightly ruffled, almost translucent quality as they mature. The strong color contrast and large leaf size make it an effective accent for brightening deeply shaded beds beneath trees or shrubs. Keep soil evenly moist and dig tubers for indoor storage before the first fall frost outside zone 9b and warmer.

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil is reliably warm; Bombshell is a compact introduction from Dr. Robert Hartman's breeding program suited to edging and small pots.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade. Bombshell carries an intense red center bleeding into a deep green margin on a compact, short-statured plant, giving concentrated color without the sprawl of larger fancy-leaf types. Its smaller stature suits edging, window boxes, and small pots where a bold color accent is wanted without overwhelming the planting. Water regularly through the growing season and lift tubers for winter storage once foliage begins to decline in fall.

common_name: Red Glamour Caladium (Dark Red Sun-Tolerant Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil is reliably warm; Red Glamour holds its dark coloring well with some direct light.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to sun, giving it a spot with at least some direct light to intensify its coloring. Red Glamour shows a dark red center laced with darker veining and rimmed in a deep green border, a richer, moodier red than the brighter scarlet of older red caladiums. Its sun-and-shade tolerance allows it to be planted in beds that receive more light than most fancy-leaf caladiums could handle without fading or scorching. Maintain consistent moisture through summer heat and dig tubers before frost outside the warmest coastal zones.

common_name: Puppy Love Caladium (Rich Deep Pink Sun-Tolerant Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers once the ground has warmed in late spring; Puppy Love is similar to the already-established Florida Sweetheart but with deeper color and thicker leaves.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to sun once the ground has warmed in late spring. Puppy Love resembles the classic strap-leaf Florida Sweetheart but carries a deeper, more saturated pink coloring on thicker, sturdier leaves that hold up better to wind and sun exposure. The narrower strap-leaf form gives a finer texture than bold fancy-leaf caladiums, useful for edging or mixed container plantings. It tolerates more direct sun than most caladiums; keep soil evenly moist and lift tubers for winter storage outside the warmest zones.

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil is reliably warm; Sweetheart is a patent-protected University of Florida-bred cultivar, distinct from the separately-established Florida Sweetheart, well suited to hanging baskets as well as garden beds.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade, spacing them to let the distinctive foliage shape show individually. Sweetheart produces bright, intensely pink leaves in a pronounced heart shape, a softer and more rounded outline than the arrow-shaped blades of most fancy-leaf caladiums. Its compact habit and vivid color make it well suited to hanging baskets and shaded containers as well as garden beds. Provide consistent moisture through the growing season and dig tubers for indoor storage before the first fall frost outside the warmest zones.
